Getting Started

is a deterministic, stream-oriented state management system written in TypeScript. It reduces boilerplate, clarifies execution flow, and provides predictable, testable, production-ready state containers called .

This guide walks you through the core concepts, the installation steps, and the fastest path to getting real application state running in a only a few lines of code.

What Problem Does Solve?

provides a simple, unified way to manage state without reducers, actions, facades, or store boilerplate. It solves:

  • State scattered across services, components, and subjects.
  • Hard-to-trace update paths and unpredictable side effects.
  • Verbose or ceremony-heavy state tools (NgRx, NGXS, Akita), or ad-hoc signals-only approaches.
  • The lack of a typed, traceable, lifecycle-aware state pipeline.

FeatureCells give you a clean, testable, maintainable state container with a fully observable lifecycle and first-class integration with Angular.

What You Get Out of the Box

FeatureCells provide:

  • A strongly-typed home for all feature state.
  • A consistent, ordered pipeline including resolve, filter, reduce, encrypt, and persist.
  • A UI-facing state wrapper powered by Angular signals or observables (StateSnapshotShape).
  • Automatic immutability and predictable state transitions.
  • Lifecycle events you can observe in provided or custom devtools.
  • Opt-in extensibility via built-in and custom (business-specific) behaviors without modifying the core FeatureCell.

FeatureCells do not require:

  • Dispatchers, actions, reducers, effect classes, or selectors.
  • Manual cleanup of subscriptions (when using signals).
  • Global stores or multi-layer indirection.
How a Fits Into Your App

A is just a small, focused state module bound to a feature domain—users, products, employees, etc. You interact with it the same way in every feature:

  • Use FeatureCell() to define it.
  • Call vault.initialize() to activate it.
  • Consume vault.state inside components as signals.
  • Call replaceState() or mergeState() to update it.

FeatureCells are intentionally small: one per feature, predictable, testable, and easy to delete or replace. They scale horizontally across features instead of vertically through global stores.

Your First FeatureCell

Let’s create the smallest possible working FeatureCell. It manages a list of employees and exposes it through Angular signals.

  1. Define your model.
  2. Create a FeatureCell service.
  3. Call vault.initialize() in the constructor.
  4. Load state using replaceState().
  5. Use the state in your components.

Yup! It's that simple. .

In the example below learn how to be up in running in minutes

Application configuration and state consumption using Angular.

Step 1: Initialize Vault and Register the FeatureCell

{{`// app.config.ts
export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    // 1️⃣ Initialize the Vault
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    // 2️⃣ Register the FeatureCell
    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeCell,
      {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: []
      },
      [
        // optional behavior array
      ],
      [
        // optional controller array
      ]
    )
  ]
};`}}

Step 2: Declare the FeatureCell Service

{{`interface Employee {
  id: number;
  name: string;
}

@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeCell {

  // Inject the FeatureCell vault once
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeCell);

  constructor() {
    // Required to activate the FeatureCell
    this.vault.initialize();
  }

  load(): void {
    this.vault.replaceState({
      loading: false,
      value: [
        { id: 1, name: 'Ada' },
        { id: 2, name: 'Brian' }
      ],
      error: null
    });
  }

  // Expose read-only state to consumers
  readonly state = this.vault.state;
}`}}

Step 3: Consume FeatureCell State in a Component

{{`@Component({...})
export class ExampleComponent {

  // Inject the FeatureCell service and read its state
  readonly employeeState = inject(EmployeeCell).state;

}`}}

Inside the component template, consumption is signal-simple:

Step 4: Render FeatureCell State in a Template

{{`@if (employeeState.isLoading()) {
  <p>Loading…</p>
} @else if (employeeState.error()) {
  <p>Error loading employees</p>
} @else if (employeeState.hasValue()) {
  {{ employeeState.value() }}
} @else {
  <p>No data</p>
}`}}

Application configuration and state consumption using React.

Step 1: Initialize Vault and Register the FeatureCell

{{`// employee.cell.ts
import { Vault, FeatureCell } from '@sdux-vault/core';

export interface Employee {
  id: number;
  name: string;
}

// 1️⃣ Initialize the Vault once at application startup
Vault({
  logLevel: 'off'
});

// 2️⃣ Register the FeatureCell at module scope
export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>({
  key: 'employees',
  initialState: []
});

// 3️⃣ Explicitly activate the FeatureCell
employeeCell.initialize();

// 4️⃣ Domain action
export function loadEmployees(): void {
  employeeCell.replaceState({
    loading: false,
    value: [
      { id: 1, name: 'Ada' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Brian' }
    ],
    error: null
  });
}

// 5️⃣ Expose read-only state access
export const employeeState = employeeCell.state;
export const employeeState$ = employeeCell.state$;`}}

Step 2: Consume FeatureCell State in a React Component

{{`// EmployeeView.tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import {
  employeeState,
  employeeState$,
  loadEmployees
} from './employee.cell';

export function EmployeeView() {
  const [snapshot, setSnapshot] = useState(employeeState);

  useEffect(() => {
    // Subscribe once on mount
    const sub = employeeState$.subscribe(setSnapshot);

    // Trigger data load (could also live elsewhere)
    loadEmployees();

    return () => sub.unsubscribe();
  }, []);

  if (snapshot.isLoading) {
    return <p>Loading…</p>;
  }

  if (snapshot.error) {
    return <p>Error: {snapshot.error.message}</p>;
  }

  if (!snapshot.hasValue) {
    return <p>No employees</p>;
  }

  return (
    <ul>
      {snapshot.value.map(emp => (
        <li key={emp.id}>{emp.name}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}`}}

Application configuration and state consumption using Vue.

Step 1: Initialize Vault and Register the FeatureCell

{{`// employee.cell.ts
import { Vault, FeatureCell } from '@sdux-vault/core';

export interface Employee {
  id: number;
  name: string;
}

// 1️⃣ Initialize the Vault once at application startup
Vault({
  logLevel: 'off'
});

// 2️⃣ Register the FeatureCell at module scope
export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<lEmployee[]>({
  key: 'employees',
  initialState: []
});

// 3️⃣ Explicitly activate the FeatureCell
employeeCell.initialize();

// 4️⃣ Domain action
export function loadEmployees(): void {
  employeeCell.replaceState({
    loading: false,
    value: [
      { id: 1, name: 'Ada' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Brian' }
    ],
    error: null
  });
}

// 5️⃣ Expose read-only state access
export const employeeState = employeeCell.state;
export const employeeState$ = employeeCell.state$;`}}

Step 2: Consume FeatureCell State in a Vue Component

{{`<l!-- EmployeeView.vue -->
<lscript setup lang="ts">
import { ref, onMounted, onBeforeUnmount } from 'vue';
import {
  employeeState,
  employeeState$,
  loadEmployees
} from './employee.cell';

// Local reactive snapshot
const snapshot = ref(employeeState);

let subscription: { unsubscribe(): void };

onMounted(() => {
  // Subscribe once when component mounts
  subscription = employeeState$.subscribe(value => {
    snapshot.value = value;
  });

  // Trigger data load (could also live elsewhere)
  loadEmployees();
});

onBeforeUnmount(() => {
  subscription?.unsubscribe();
});
<l/script>

<ltemplate>
  <lp v-if="snapshot.isLoading">Loading…<l/p>

  <lp v-else-if="snapshot.error">
    Error: {{ snapshot.error.message }}
  <l/p>

  <lp v-else-if="!snapshot.hasValue">No employees<l/p>

  <lul v-else>
    <lli v-for="emp in snapshot.value" :key="emp.id">
      {{ emp.name }}
    <l/li>
  <l/ul>
<l/template>`}}
Understanding replaceState() and mergeState()

The two primary state update APIs are:

replaceState

Replaces the entire FeatureCell snapshot. Used for bootstrapping, resetting, or loading new data. 

{{`// Full state replacement
this.vault.replaceState({
  loading: false,
  value: employees,
  error: null
});`}}
 
{{`// Full state replacement
employeeCell.replaceState({
  loading: false,
  value: employees,
  error: null
});`}}
 
{{`// Full state replacement
employeeCell.replaceState({
  loading: false,
  value: employees,
  error: null
});`}}

mergeState

Merges partial values into the existing state snapshot. Used for incremental updates such as toggling flags or appending values.

Merge behavior is configurable via additional built-in or custom merge behaviors. 

{{`// Shallow state merge
this.vault.mergeState({
  value: [...prevEmployees, newEmployee]
});`}}
 
{{`// Shallow state merge
employeeCell.mergeState({
  value: [...prevEmployees, newEmployee]
});`}}
 
{{`// Full state replacement
employeeCell.replaceState({
  loading: false,
  value: employees,
  error: null
});`}}
When to Use

Use SDuX when…

  • You want predictable state transitions.
  • You're tired of boilerplate and action-based flux systems.
  • You want Angular signals at the core, not the edge.
  • You want FeatureCells as clean, isolated state modules.

Don't use SDuX when…

  • You just need a single signal for local component state.
  • Your feature has no meaningful state transitions.
  • You need global NgRx-style entity maps. SDuX prioritizes lightweight, feature-scoped state.
Performance Notes
  • All state operations are synchronous and extremely fast.
  • Signals allow zero-subscription UI updates.
  • Heavy transforms can be pushed into reducers to keep update logic centralized.
  • No zone.js overhead—everything is signal-driven.
Testing Guidance
  • Unit-test logic directly by calling replaceState()/mergeState().
  • Use the InsightService to inspect pipeline emissions.
  • Integration-test the entire update flow using a real FeatureCell.
  • State access is signals-based—no cleanup needed.
Best Practices
  • Create one FeatureCell per feature domain.
  • Call initialize() immediately in the constructor.
  • Avoid calling replace/merge directly from components—wrap in methods.
  • Use reducers for domain-specific transformations.
  • Use mergeState for lists and incremental updates.
